speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of relief with defecation, urgency, and tenesmus are highly suggestive of Inflammatory Bowel Disease, but your camping history raises concern for infectious colitis. Was the illness at the campsite also accompanied by fever or bloody stools, and do you have a history of similar episodes in the past? speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming that other campers also became ill. speaker: Doctor
text: The normal blood work and inflammatory markers make inflammatory bowel disease unlikely, and your camping history with sick contacts strongly suggests an infectious etiology. speaker: Doctor
text: The normal stool studies and imaging are reassuring; however, your symptoms of urgent, mucus-containing diarrhea relieved by defecation are classic for Irritable Bowel Syndrome with diarrhea (IBS-D), especially since infectious causes have been ruled out. Can you confirm if your bowel habits have changed in the year before these symptoms started, and have you noticed any anxiety or stress correlating with your flare-ups?
